physics: bin piles are rigid-body settled (Blender Bullet), copies carry final transforms; hung bundles pinned on a cord
coordinates: Unity prefab space, same origin as MeatRack.obj. From Blender (z-up, -y front): ux=-bx, uy=bz, uz=-by. box_size is (x, y, z) in Unity axes. Rotation matrices convert as R_u = M R_b M^T with M the same map; euler values are Unity order (Z, then X, then Y).
placing_an_item: For every copy: scale the stored item's model uniformly so the longest side of its renderer bounds equals longest_m; rotate it with align (turn its longest bounds axis to long_axis_to and its thinnest bounds axis to thin_axis_to, middle axis follows right-handed), then apply then_rotate (about the unit centre axes); put the centre of its bounds at unit.position + copy.offset. rendered_rotation_* is the finished rotation for the item used in the render (render_item) and can be used directly for items with a similar shape. ROUND 3: pile units (bins) hold SETTLED copies from a rigid body simulation: their then_rotate is identity and align alone gives the final rotation, offset is the final resting position (items touch, nothing floats); fill is cumulative, so copies already settled never move when more units are shown. Within a unit the copies are in drop order. Bundle units also carry a cord (hemp box from the hook knot down through the bundle) with knots; the items touch it.
fill_order: units are sorted in fill order: show the first k units for k stacks in use (one stack per unit, stack holding the same item for all copies of a unit).
note: r5 (Joost, 22 Oct: 'the lox meat is way too small'): the 40 hook units are round 4's unchanged; the 24 bin units are re-settled with RawMeat at 0.40x true size (longest 0.246 m, 2 per pile) instead of eight NeckTail copies at 0.15 m; crop_layouts put every known meat, fish, egg and animal part in the bins near true size (meatrack_r5.py).

crop_layouts_doc: crop_layouts: one physics-settled full bin per item (item prefab name). A bin holding n stacks of an item shows stacks[0..n-1] of that item's layout (all of a stack's copies), so filling never moves earlier copies (stack k was dropped onto stacks 0..k-1 after they were frozen). Per copy: the item's model in the mod's item space (ItemVisual: prefab root space without the root's own scale, which is 1 for every one of these items, turned 180 degrees about up), scaled uniformly by 'scale' (= x the item's true size), rotated by rot_quat_xyzw about its ItemVisual bounds centre, that centre put at crate_floor_centres[bin] + offset (prefab space, Unity y-up/+z front; offset is bin-floor-centre local). Exactly the mod's crop path (pos = centre - r * (s * Bounds.center)); item_bounds is the Bounds the mod measures (centre and size in item space), used for the offsets. Settled in one generic bin (0.392 x 0.412 inside, corner posts, heap ceiling 0.30 m over the floor) and checked against the real frame in all six bins. Per item also: true_size_m (Unity x, y, z at scale 1), true_longest_m, mode, copies_per_stack, check (copies, dropped, float_worst_mm, clipping_in_6_bins, heap_top_m above the floor). crate_floor_centres: by bin index (the units' 'bin' field). No '_generic' layout on purpose: an item without one (blood clot, blood bag, modded) takes the bin units' own copies, whose align/longest_m turn it like the demo item and whose floor rule keeps it out of the floor.

crop_layouts_scale_exceptions.rule: 0.60 x true size for every item, except: (1) a lying item gets the largest scale that lies across the 0.39 m bin with 8 degrees of yaw play, a tumbled one the largest that fits the bin and the heap ceiling; (2) an item whose full bin (4 stacks x copies_per_stack) did not settle was settled again at 6% less scale until it did.

physics_r5: Blender rigid body (Bullet), rootbin_r5's settings: items = active convex hulls of the item, friction 0.8, restitution 0, damping 0.50/0.95, margin 1.5 mm, substeps 20, iterations 40; one copy per item per batch, settled then frozen; stack order back-left, front-right, back-right, front-left. A try is re-dropped when a body is farther than 5 mm from its support (floor, an earlier copy, or a wall it leans on) or any vertex leaves the cavity or rises over the ceiling.
